definition_en: to learn about a subject, to examine something carefully, or a room used for reading and writing
core_image: 一盏台灯下摊开的书，旁边放着写满字的笔记本
scene: 她每天晚上学习两个小时。She studies for two hours every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 study 是「学习」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她每天晚上学习两个小时。

senses.title: Learn a subject
senses.definition: to spend time learning about a subject
senses.definitionCN: 花时间学习某一科目
senses.example: She studies for two hours every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天晚上学习两个小时。
senses.why: This is the everyday learning sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的学习义项。

senses.title: Examine carefully
senses.definition: to examine something carefully to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 仔细考察某事物以理解它
senses.example: The team studied the problem for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 团队研究这个问题研究了好几个星期。
senses.why: Learning turns outward to the world.
senses.whyCN: 学习在这里转向了外部世界。

senses.title: A reading room
senses.definition: a room in a house used for reading and writing
senses.definitionCN: 家中用于读书写作的房间
senses.example: He keeps his books in the study.
senses.exampleCN: 他把书放在书房里。
senses.why: The action gets a room of its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作有了自己的房间。

intro.en: Study comes from Latin studium, eagerness, through Old French.
intro.cn: study 来自拉丁语 studium（热忱），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Studium meant eager effort.
items.cn: studium 意为热切的努力。

items.en: Estudie named study and care.
items.cn: estudie 指钻研与用心。

items.en: Studie meant to learn or examine.
items.cn: 中古英语 studie 意为学习或考察。

items.en: Study also named a room for books.
items.cn: study 也指放书的房间。

items.en: Case study named a close examination.
items.cn: case study 指个案研究。

note.en: Study is compared with look-alike words and with words for learning.
note.cn: 把 study 与形近词以及表示学习的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Study is effort turned toward knowledge, and the room that holds it.

normal.en: He studies history at university.
normal.cn: 他在大学学习历史。

normal.en: We studied the map before leaving.

normal.en: She studies hard for exams.
normal.cn: 她为考试努力学习。

normal.en: The report is a case study.
normal.cn: 这份报告是一个个案研究。

normal.en: The study was warm and quiet.
normal.cn: 书房里温暖而安静。

abstract.en: Study is a conversation with people you never meet.
abstract.cn: 学习，是和从未谋面的人交谈。

abstract.en: The more we study, the more we see.
abstract.cn: 研究得越多，看见的就越多。

abstract.en: A quiet room can hold a loud idea.
abstract.cn: 安静的房间，能装下响亮的思想。

examples.en: She studies for two hours every evening.
examples.cn: 她每天晚上学习两个小时。

examples.en: The team studied the problem for weeks.
examples.cn: 团队研究这个问题研究了好几个星期。

dict_mnemonic.text: study 的核心是「用心钻研」；在学校用心是学习，对一个问题用心是研究，专门用来用心的房间就是书房。

root: 来自拉丁语 studium（热忱、钻研），经古法语 estudie 进入英语；由学习与考察的动作，引申为研究，再指家中读书写作的书房。

sensesIntro.en: Study is learning, careful research, or the room where both happen.
sensesIntro.cn: study 是学习、仔细研究，或让这两件事发生的书房。

core.en: A lamp, a book, and a page filling with notes.
core.cn: 一盏灯、一本书、一页渐渐写满的笔记。

branches.en: A student reads until midnight.
branches.cn: 学生读到半夜。

branches.en: A team checks every detail.
branches.cn: 团队核查每个细节。

branches.en: Books line a quiet room.
branches.cn: 书排满一间安静的房间。

branches.en: Reading turns into finding out.
branches.cn: 阅读变成了探究。

branches.en: The room and the work share a name.
branches.cn: 房间与工作共用一个名字。

definition_en: things in general, the material something is made of, or to fill something tightly
core_image: 一个塞得鼓鼓的背包，里面装着各种说不上名字的东西
scene: 他把衣服塞进背包里。He stuffed his clothes into the backpack.
sceneCN: 这里 stuff 是「填塞」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他把衣服塞进背包里。

senses.title: Things in general
senses.definition: a word for things when the exact name is not needed
senses.definitionCN: 不必说出确切名称时对物品的统称
senses.example: Put your stuff in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的东西放到角落里。
senses.why: This is the catch-all noun.
senses.whyCN: 这是包罗万象的名词。

senses.title: Material
senses.definition: the substance something is made of
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物的物质
senses.example: This stuff feels like wool.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料摸起来像羊毛。
senses.why: The general noun becomes a substance.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的名词在这里变成了具体的物质。

senses.title: Fill tightly
senses.definition: to fill something tightly with things
senses.definitionCN: 把东西紧紧地塞进某物
senses.example: He stuffed his clothes into the backpack.
senses.exampleCN: 他把衣服塞进背包里。
senses.why: Material pressed into a space becomes a verb.
senses.whyCN: 把材料压进空间，就成了动词。

normal.en: My stuff is in the car.

abstract.en: Stuff is what remains when names run out.

abstract.en: A full bag is a small argument with space.

abstract.en: Knowing your stuff needs no loud voice.

definition_en: the topic being discussed, a course of study, a person studied, or being affected by something
core_image: 被放在讨论中央、供人观看与研究的那个东西
scene: 今天这节课的主题是天气。The subject of today's lesson is the weather.

senses.title: Topic

definition_zh: 潜艇；海面之下的（作名词指潜艇，作形容词指水下的、海底的）
definition_en: a warship that can travel under the sea; also an adjective meaning beneath the sea
core_image: 一艘细长的黑色艇体沉入水中，只留潜望镜划开水面，四周立刻安静下来
scene: 潜艇在洋脊旁缓缓下潜，螺旋桨搅起细小的气泡。The submarine dived quietly beside the research ship.
sceneCN: 这里 submarine 指「可潜航的舰艇」（第 1 个义项：作为船只的潜艇）；句意为这艘潜艇在考察船旁悄然下潜。

pos.zh: 海面之下的；海底的（多作定语，如 submarine cable、submarine canyon）

collocations.zh: 潜艇三明治（长条夹心面包）

derivatives.zh: submarine + -er（从事者后缀）→ 潜艇艇员：在潜艇上服役的人
sub-（在下）+ mergere（拉丁「沉入」）+ -sion（名词后缀）→ 浸没、下潜：沉入水下的动作或状态
sub- + mergere + -ible（能……的）→ 可潜航器；能潜入水下的
submarine（潜艇）+ sandwich（三明治）→ 潜艇三明治：形似艇体的长条夹心面包
anti-（希腊「对抗」）+ submarine（潜艇）→ 反潜的：用于对付潜艇的

senses.title: A diving warship
senses.definition: a vessel designed to operate beneath the surface
senses.definitionCN: 设计为在水面之下运作的船只
senses.example: The submarine dived quietly beside the research ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘潜艇在考察船旁悄然下潜。
senses.why: sub- 'under' plus marinus 'of the sea' literally means 'undersea', and the noun applies that to a craft.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下」加 marinus「海的」字面就是「海下」，名词把这个意思用在船只上。

senses.title: The submarine force
senses.definition: the branch of a navy that operates submarines, or its crews
senses.definitionCN: 海军中运作潜艇的兵种，或指其艇员
senses.example: Submarine crews train for months before deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 潜艇艇员在部署前训练数月。
senses.why: a fleet branch is named by its main equipment, so the word also stands for the service.
senses.whyCN: 兵种常以主要装备命名，因此这个词也代表该兵种。

senses.title: Beneath the sea, as an adjective
senses.definition: existing or occurring below the sea surface
senses.definitionCN: 存在于海面之下或发生在海面之下
senses.example: Submarine cables carry most international internet traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 海底电缆承载大部分国际互联网流量。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the literal sense of the Latin parts and attaches to whatever lies under the sea.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留拉丁成分的字面义，附在任何位于海面之下的事物上。

senses.title: Seafloor geology
senses.definition: the adjective used for canyons, fans and ridges on the seafloor
senses.definitionCN: 用于海床上的峡谷、扇体与洋脊的形容词
senses.example: The submarine canyon feeds a fan of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海底峡谷养出一片砂质扇体。
senses.why: geology needed a short modifier for features hidden under water, and reused the existing adjective.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个简短限定词来指藏在海水之下的地貌，于是复用了现成的形容词。

senses.title: Submarine cable engineering
senses.definition: the adjective for cables, pipes and structures laid on the seabed
senses.definitionCN: 用于铺设在海床上的电缆、管道与结构的形容词
senses.example: A submarine cable links the island to the mainland.
senses.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆把该岛与大陆相连。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrowed the adjective to installed infrastructure rather than ships.
senses.whyCN: 工程义把这个形容词收窄到已安装的基础设施，而非船只。

senses.title: The long sandwich
senses.titleCN: 潜艇三明治：长条夹心面包
senses.definition: a long roll split and filled, named for its shape
senses.definitionCN: 剖开夹馅的长条面包，因形状得名
senses.example: He ordered a submarine with cheese and ham.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一份夹奶酪与火腿的潜艇三明治。
senses.why: a long filled roll resembles a hull, so American English borrowed the vessel's name for the food.
senses.whyCN: 长条夹馅面包形似艇体，因此美式英语借船名来称这种食物。

senses.title: The underhand pitch
senses.definition: a baseball pitch delivered with the arm below the shoulder
senses.definitionCN: 手臂低于肩部投出的棒球球路
senses.example: The reliever throws with a submarine motion.
senses.exampleCN: 这名后援投手以下手动作投球。
senses.why: the low arm slot is figuratively beneath the usual plane, so baseball borrowed the sea word.
senses.whyCN: 低臂位在通常平面之下，因此棒球借用了这个海词。

senses.title: Hidden and silent action
senses.definition: the quality of moving unseen and unheard, as a submarine does
senses.definitionCN: 像潜艇那样不被看见、不被听见地行动
senses.example: The campaign ran like a submarine, silent until it surfaced.
senses.exampleCN: 这场行动像潜艇一样，一直无声，直到浮出水面。
senses.why: a submarine's military value is invisibility, so the word became a metaphor for concealed action.
senses.whyCN: 潜艇的军事价值在于不可见，因此这个词成为隐蔽行动的隐喻。

intro.en: Submarine is Latin in its parts: sub- 'under' plus marinus 'of the sea', from mare 'sea'. It entered English as an adjective in the seventeenth century and became a noun for the vessel at the end of the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: submarine 的各成分都是拉丁语：sub-「在下」加 marinus「海的」，后者来自 mare「海」。它于十七世纪以形容词进入英语，到十九世纪末成为指舰船的名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below' and is the prefix in submerge, subsoil and submarine.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，是 submerge、subsoil 与 submarine 的前缀。

items.en: Mare 'sea' produced marinus 'of the sea', the source of the -marine part.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，即 -marine 部分的来源。

items.en: Submarine first described things living or lying beneath the sea, not ships.
items.cn: submarine 最初描述生活在海面之下或位于海面之下的事物，并非船只。

items.en: Experimental submarines appeared in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, but the noun submarine for a warship settled in English around 1900.
items.cn: 实验性潜水器在十七、十八世纪出现，但指军舰的名词 submarine 约于一九零零年在英语中定型。

items.en: Two world wars made submarine a common word for the warship, and engineering extended it to cables and geology.
items.cn: 两次世界大战使 submarine 成为军舰的常用词，工程又把它扩展到电缆与地质。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): dates for the first noun use vary between 1899 and the early 1900s, and no single citation is universally accepted.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：名词首次使用的年代在各家著作中自一八九九年至二十世纪初不等，没有公认的唯一书证。

note.en: Group one holds the vessels and craft most often confused with a submarine; group two holds the adjectives for things beneath the sea.
note.cn: 第一组是常与潜艇混淆的船只与潜器；第二组是表示海面之下的形容词。

entries.definition: A small craft carried by a ship and used for research or repair; it usually has no long-range independent patrol.
entries.definitionCN: 由母船携带、用于研究或修理的小型潜器；通常不能独立远航巡逻。

entries.definition: A person who works or swims underwater; it is human, not a vessel.

entries.definition: Any naval vessel built for combat; a submarine is one kind of warship, not the general term.

entries.definition: A long filled roll named for its hull-like shape; it has no connection to naval vessels beyond the metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 因形似艇体而得名的长条夹馅面包；除比喻外与军舰无关。

entries.definition: Beneath the sea, used of the seabed and its features; it is an adjective and cannot name the vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 海面之下，用于海床及其地貌；只是形容词，不能命名舰船。

entries.definition: Below the surface of any water, fresh or salt; it is broader and not naval.
entries.definitionCN: 任何水体表面之下，淡水或咸水；范围更宽，且非海军用语。

entries.definition: Living or occurring partly under water; it is biological and rare, not a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 部分在水下生活或发生的；属生物学用语且罕见，不指船只。

entries.definition: Covered by water, often after sinking; a submarine is submerged by design, but the adjective alone implies no crew or engine.
entries.definitionCN: 被水覆盖，常因沉没；潜艇是设计上被淹没，但单用该形容词不暗示船员或动力。

normal.en: A submarine's weapon is silence: it is dangerous because it cannot be seen.

abstract.en: It moves through the sea the way a thought moves through silence.

root: 来自拉丁语 subsequi（跟随在后）的分词 subsequens，由 sub（在后）与 sequi（跟随）组合；字面是「跟在后面的」，因此表示随后的、后来的。

sensesIntro.en: Subsequent means coming after something, or later in a series.
sensesIntro.cn: subsequent 表示在某事之后发生的，或在一系列中较晚的。

core.en: The next step behind the one just taken.
core.cn: 刚迈出的一步之后的下一步。

branches.en: A subsequent meeting changed the plan.
branches.cn: 随后的一次会议改变了计划。

branches.en: Subsequent studies confirmed the result.
branches.cn: 后来的研究证实了这一结果。

branches.en: Time order and series order share one word.
branches.cn: 时间上的先后和序列中的先后共用一个词。

branches.en: The subsequent years were quiet.
branches.cn: 随后的几年很平静。

branches.en: The decision was made subsequent to the report.
branches.cn: 这个决定是在报告之后作出的。

intro.en: Subsequent takes -ly and shares its root with sequence and sequel.
intro.cn: subsequent 可加 -ly，并与 sequence、sequel 同根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base sequ- meant to follow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 sequ- 意为跟随。

items.example: The subsequence appears in the data.
Prices rose and the consequent panic followed.
items.exampleCN: 价格上涨，随之而来的是恐慌。

items.example: It rained and consequently we stayed in.
items.exampleCN: 下雨了，因此我们待在室内。

items.example: The sequel was better than the film.
items.exampleCN: 续集比第一部电影更好。

items.example: Subsequent to the meeting, she called.

latinEntries.example: Sequi gave English sequence and subsequent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sequi 演变为英语的 sequence 和 subsequent。

definition_zh: 子公司；附属机构；辅助的；附属的；补充的
definition_en: a company controlled by another company, or, as an adjective, serving in a secondary or supporting role
core_image: 后备队列站在主力身后：不冲在最前，却随时补位
scene: 集团总部把新收购的小厂挂在自己名下，小厂另立法人，账目却并进总表。The group kept the small plant as a subsidiary with its own legal name and one consolidated balance sheet.
sceneCN: 这里 subsidiary 是「子公司」（第 1 个义项：由另一家公司控股、但仍是独立法人的公司）；句意：集团把那家小厂留作子公司，它有独立的法律名称，账目则合并进同一张总表。

pos.zh: 子公司；附属机构；下属单位
辅助的；附属的；补充的；次要的

derivatives.zh: 与 subsidiary 同出 subsidium，义为「补贴；补助金」，是同一词根的另一个分支
由 subsidy 加 -ize 构成，义为「补贴；资助」
由 subsidiary 加 -ity 构成，义为「辅助原则」，指上级只在必要时介入
由 subsidiary 加 -ly 构成，义为「辅助地；次要地」

senses.title: A company owned by another
senses.definition: a separate legal company whose controlling shares are held by a parent company
senses.definitionCN: 股权由母公司控制、但自身仍是独立法人的公司
senses.example: The bank set up a subsidiary in Hong Kong to hold the loans.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行在香港设立了一家子公司来持有这些贷款。
senses.why: Subsidium was the reserve force kept behind the line, and a controlled company stands behind its parent in the same supporting position.
senses.whyCN: subsidium 是留在阵线后方的后备力量，受控公司正以同样的支援姿态站在母公司身后。

senses.title: A dependent organization
senses.definition: an organization that depends on a larger body, such as a branch school or a subsidiary hospital
senses.definitionCN: 依附于更大机构的组织，如附属学校、附属医院
senses.example: The museum runs a subsidiary in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆在老城区办了一个附属展馆。
senses.why: The reserve image does not require a company, so any dependent body can be called a subsidiary.
senses.whyCN: 「后备」意象并不限于公司，任何依附性机构都可以叫 subsidiary。

senses.title: Serving in a secondary role
senses.definition: having a less important role that supports something else
senses.definitionCN: 作用较次要、用于支持别的事物
senses.example: Price was a subsidiary reason for choosing that supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 价格是选择那家供应商的一个次要原因。
senses.why: so the adjective means supporting rather than central.
senses.whyCN: 站在阵线后方的东西是在支援前方，所以形容词义是「辅助的」而非核心的。

senses.title: Attached and subordinate
senses.definition: used before a noun for something attached to a main body and subject to it
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指附属于主体并受其支配的事物
senses.example: The subsidiary company files its own tax return.
senses.exampleCN: 这家附属公司自行申报纳税。
senses.why: The noun sense lends the adjective its legal edge, naming whatever hangs from a main entity.
senses.whyCN: 名词义给形容词带来法律色彩，指从属于主体的一切。

senses.title: Supplementary, not essential
senses.definition: added to support a main thing, as in a subsidiary ledger or subsidiary evidence
senses.definitionCN: 附加在主要事物之旁以示支持，如明细账或辅助证据
senses.example: The auditor checked the subsidiary ledger against the main account.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师把明细账与总账核对了一遍。
senses.why: A reserve is not the main army but it completes it, so the word also means supplementary.
senses.whyCN: 后备力量不是主力，却把主力补全，所以这个词也有「补充」义。

senses.title: The group of controlled companies
senses.definition: the whole set of controlled companies belonging to one parent, taken as a group
senses.definitionCN: 同一母公司旗下所有受控公司构成的整体
senses.example: The parent and its subsidiaries report as one group.
senses.exampleCN: 母公司与其子公司作为一个集团合并报告。
senses.why: In group accounting the plural names the collection, the ring of reserve units around one centre.
senses.whyCN: 在集团会计里，复数形式指这一整圈围绕一个中心的后备单位。

intro.en: Subsidiary comes from Latin subsidium, the reserve troops kept behind the battle line, through the adjective subsidiarius.
intro.cn: subsidiary 来自拉丁语 subsidium（留在战线后方的后备部队），经形容词 subsidiarius 进入英语。

items.en: Subsidium means the troops held in reserve behind the line.
items.cn: subsidium 意为留在阵线后方的后备部队。

items.en: The word is generally explained as sub-, under, plus sedere, to sit, a force sitting behind.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词由 sub-（在下）加 sedere（坐）构成，即坐在后方的一支力量。

items.en: Subsidiarius means serving as a reserve or as help.
items.cn: subsidiarius 意为充当后备或援助的。

items.en: Subsidium also means help or relief in ordinary prose.
items.cn: 在一般文献里，subsidium 也指援助、救助。

items.en: Subsidiary enters English as an adjective meaning auxiliary.
items.cn: subsidiary 进入英语时是形容词，意为辅助的。

items.en: Company law gives the word its corporate sense of a controlled firm.
items.cn: 公司法赋予这个词「受控公司」的企业义。

note.en: Subsidiary belongs to the reserve family of subsidium, and in business it stands beside affiliate, branch, and its opposite, the parent company.
note.cn: subsidiary 属于 subsidium 的「后备」词族，在商业语境里与 affiliate、branch 并列，并与反义的 parent company 相对。

entries.definition: money paid by a government to support a price or an industry
entries.definitionCN: 政府为支持价格或产业而支付的补助金，同出 subsidium

entries.definition: to support something with money
in a supporting or secondary way
a company linked to another by ownership or agreement
entries.definitionCN: 关联公司；因股权或协议而与另一家公司相连

entries.definition: a local office of a firm, without separate legal identity
entries.definitionCN: 分公司；分支机构，本身不是独立法人

entries.definition: the company that controls a subsidiary
entries.definitionCN: 母公司；控制子公司的公司，与子公司相对

normalIntro.en: Subsidiary keeps the picture of reserve troops: they stand behind the front line, ready to help but never the centre of the battle.
normalIntro.cn: subsidiary 保留着后备部队的画面：站在前线之后，随时支援，却从不是战场的中心。

normal.en: Subsidium was the reserve force behind the line.
normal.cn: subsidium 就是阵线后方的后备力量。

normal.en: A subsidiary company stands behind its parent the way reserves stand behind the front.
normal.cn: 子公司站在母公司身后，正如后备军站在前线之后。

normal.en: A wholly owned subsidiary is one whose shares all belong to the parent.
normal.cn: wholly owned subsidiary 就是股份全归母公司所有的子公司。

normal.en: A subsidiary ledger supports the main account.
normal.cn: subsidiary ledger 是用来支持总账的明细账。

normal.en: Compare subsidy: both words come from reserve help, but one is money and one is a body.
normal.cn: 对比 subsidy：两词都出自「后备援助」，一个指钱，一个指机构。

abstract.en: Picture a second row of soldiers half a step behind the first.
abstract.cn: 想象第二排士兵站在第一排之后半步。

abstract.en: Picture a small office with its own doorplate but the same owner upstairs.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小办公室，有自己的门牌，楼上却是同一个东家。

abstract.en: Picture a footnote page pinned under the main page of a report.
abstract.cn: 想象报告正文下面钉着一页附表。

examples.en: The group sold its subsidiary in Brazil last year.
examples.cn: 集团去年卖掉了在巴西的子公司。

examples.en: Each subsidiary keeps its own board and its own accounts.
examples.cn: 每家子公司都有自己的董事会和自己的账目。

examples.en: Cost was a subsidiary concern; reliability mattered more.
examples.cn: 成本只是次要考虑，可靠性更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆词联想：sub（在下）加 sid（坐）加 iary——坐在下面、随时补位的那一排，就是后备，也就是子公司；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 subsidium（留在阵线后方的后备部队，一般认为由 sub-「在下」加 sedere「坐」构成）→ 形容词 subsidiarius（后备的、辅助的）→ 英语 subsidiary，核心义「站在后面待命支援的一方」，故有「辅助的」与「子公司」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Subsidiary begins with the controlled company, widens to any dependent body, then turns adjectival for auxiliary and attached things, adds the supplementary sense, and ends with the group of controlled companies.
sensesIntro.cn: subsidiary 先指受控公司，扩展到任何依附性机构，再转为形容词表示辅助与附属，又添出补充义，最后指整个子公司群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reserve line standing half a step behind the front, ready to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在前线之后半步的后备队列，随时可以补上。

branches.en: The controlled company is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 受控公司是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: Any dependent body can wear the same name.
branches.cn: 任何依附性机构都能用同一个名称。

branches.en: The adjective of auxiliary role comes straight from the reserve image.
branches.cn: 「辅助」的形容词义直接来自后备意象。

branches.en: The attributive sense marks legal attachment to a main body.
branches.cn: 定语义标示对主体的法律隶属关系。

branches.en: Supplementary records and the whole subsidiary group are the two accounting edges.
branches.cn: 补充性的账册与整个子公司群，是这个词在会计上的两个边缘。

intro.en: Subsidiary is built from Latin subsidium and the adjective ending -arius, with English -ary, -ly, -ity, and the parallel noun subsidy.
intro.cn: subsidiary 由拉丁语 subsidium 加形容词词尾 -arius 构成，英语里再带出 -ary、-ly、-ity，并有平行的名词 subsidy。

latinIntro.en: Latin subsidium means the reserve kept behind the line; subsidiarius means serving as a reserve or help.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 subsidium 意为留在阵线后方的后备队；subsidiarius 意为充当后备或援助的。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the force behind the line.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把这支力量放在阵线之后。

items.example: Sedere builds the picture of troops sitting in reserve.
items.exampleCN: sedere 构成后备部队「坐着待命」的画面。

items.example: Subsidiarius is the direct Latin adjective.
items.exampleCN: subsidiarius 是直接的拉丁语形容词。

items.example: The noun carries the corporate sense.
Subsidy is the money branch of the same root.
items.exampleCN: subsidy 是同一词根的「钱」分支。

definition_zh: 补贴；补助金；（历史）议会拨给王室的款项；后备援助
definition_en: money paid by a government or authority to support an industry, keep prices low, or help a person or group
core_image: 后方粮车上备好的粮袋，前线缺粮时立刻推上前去
scene: 麦收前价格下跌，政府给种植小麦的农户发了一笔钱，让他们不至于亏本。The government paid a subsidy to wheat farmers to keep prices stable.
sceneCN: 这里 subsidy 是「政府补贴」（第 1 个义项：政府为支持生产或稳定价格而支付的款项）；句意：政府向麦农发放补贴以稳定价格。

derivatives.zh: 由 subsidy 加后缀 -ize 构成，指给予补贴、资助
由 subsidize 加 -ed 构成，指受补贴的
由 subsidize 加 -ation 构成，指补贴行为
同源于拉丁语 subsidiarius，指辅助的、次要的；作名词指子公司

senses.title: Government support for an industry
senses.definition: money a government pays to producers or sellers to lower prices or protect an industry
senses.definitionCN: 政府支付给生产者或销售者、用以降低价格或保护产业的款项
senses.example: The government offered a subsidy to keep bread prices low.
senses.exampleCN: 政府提供补贴以压低面包价格。
senses.why: The Latin source names troops held in reserve, money set behind the line to be used when needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源指留在后方的后备队，即备在战线之后、需要时动用的钱。

senses.title: A grant to a person or body
senses.definition: a sum granted to a person, family, or institution to help with costs
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人、家庭或机构以帮助支付费用的款项
senses.example: The charity received a subsidy for its housing project.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为其住房项目获得了一笔补助金。
senses.why: From public money for industry the word extends to any grant that covers a gap.
senses.whyCN: 从支持产业的公共资金，这个词扩展到任何填补缺口的补助。

senses.title: A parliamentary grant to the Crown
senses.definition: a sum voted by Parliament to the sovereign for public purposes
senses.definitionCN: 议会为公共用途拨给君主的款项
senses.example: In the seventeenth century Parliament voted a subsidy to the king.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪时，议会投票通过拨给国王一笔款项。
senses.why: English history gave subsidy a precise legal sense: money voted to the Crown.
senses.whyCN: 英国历史赋予 subsidy 一个精确的法律含义：议会拨给王室的款项。

senses.title: Money for allied troops
senses.definition: money paid to an ally to hire soldiers or support a war
senses.definitionCN: 支付给盟国以雇用士兵或支持战争的款项
senses.example: The treaty promised a subsidy for the allied army.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺为盟军提供一笔款项。
senses.why: The oldest military sense survives: reserve troops paid from a supporting fund.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的军事义项仍在：由支援款项支付的后备军队。

senses.title: Help or support in general
senses.definition: support or aid given to a person or cause
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人或事业的援助与支持
senses.example: The plan relies on a subsidy from private donors.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划依靠私人捐助者的资助。
senses.why: The monetary sense lightens into general help, keeping the idea of support from behind.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义淡化了一般的帮助，但仍保留「从后方支援」的意思。

intro.en: Subsidy comes from Latin subsidium, reserve troops or help, from sub, behind, and sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: subsidy 来自拉丁语 subsidium（后备队、援助），由 sub（在后）与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Subsidium first names troops kept in reserve behind the line.
items.cn: subsidium 最初指留在战线后方的后备队。

items.en: It is built from sub, behind, and sedere, to sit.
items.cn: 它由 sub（在后）与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Subside carries the sense of help or support into French.
items.cn: subside 把「援助、支持」的含义带入法语。

items.en: Subsidy enters English as money granted by Parliament.
items.cn: subsidy 以「议会拨付的款项」进入英语。

items.en: Modern use adds state aid to industry and to households.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了国家对产业与家庭的援助。

note.en: Subsidy is the noun of money held in reserve, close to its verb family and to words for grants.
note.cn: subsidy 是表示「留作后备的钱」的名词，与它的动词词族以及表示补助的词相邻。

entries.definition: to pay a subsidy to
supported by a subsidy
auxiliary or secondary; a branch company
money given for a particular purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途提供的款项；拨款

entries.definition: a regular sum paid to help with costs
entries.definitionCN: 为帮助支付费用而定期给予的款项

entries.definition: help or support given to a person or country
entries.definitionCN: 给予个人或国家的援助

normalIntro.en: Subsidy is money kept behind the line, ready to support whatever is short in front.
normalIntro.cn: subsidy 是备在战线后方的钱，随时支援前方短缺之处。

normal.en: The Latin root is reserve troops, money waiting behind the front.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根是后备队，即在前线后方待命的钱。

normal.en: A subsidy is paid by a government, not earned in a sale.
normal.cn: subsidy 由政府支付，而不是在交易中赚得。

normal.en: Farm subsidies keep food prices from falling too low.
normal.cn: 农业补贴防止食品价格跌得过低。

normal.en: The verb is subsidize: to pay such a grant.
normal.cn: 动词是 subsidize，意为支付这类补贴。

normal.en: Keep subsidy and subsidiary apart: the first is the money, the second is a branch company.
normal.cn: 要分清 subsidy 与 subsidiary：前者是钱，后者是子公司。

abstract.en: Picture a grain cart kept behind the front line.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆停在前线后方的粮车。

abstract.en: Imagine a sealed envelope with money for a family in need.
abstract.cn: 想象一个装着钱、寄给困难家庭的密封信封。

abstract.en: Think of a chest of coins voted to the king in Parliament.
abstract.cn: 想象一箱在议会投票通过后拨给国王的钱币。

examples.en: The government cut the subsidy on fossil fuels last year.
examples.cn: 政府去年削减了化石燃料补贴。

examples.en: Farmers depend on a subsidy to survive a bad harvest.
examples.cn: 农民依靠补贴度过歉收。

examples.en: The city offers a subsidy for new solar panels.
examples.cn: 这座城市为新太阳能板提供补贴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨布赛迪」——听上去像「撒补贴」，政府往你兜里撒钱；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在后）+ sedere（坐）→ subsidium（坐在后方的后备队、援助）→ 英语 subsidy（援助→议会拨款→政府补贴），核心义「留在后方、随时补上的支援」。

sensesIntro.en: Subsidy begins as reserve troops, becomes a grant of money voted by Parliament, then state aid to industry, then any grant or general support.
sensesIntro.cn: subsidy 从后备军队起步，变为议会拨付的款项，再指国家对产业的补贴，最后泛指补助与支持。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grain cart waiting behind the front line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆停在前线后方待命的粮车。

branches.en: State aid to producers is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 国家对生产者的补贴是核心的现代义项。

branches.en: A grant to a person or body widens the same money idea.
branches.cn: 给个人或机构的补助金拓宽了同一种金钱观念。

branches.en: The parliamentary grant is the precise historical sense.
branches.cn: 议会拨款是精确的历史义项。

branches.en: Money for allied troops keeps the oldest military image.
branches.cn: 雇用盟军的款项保留了最古老的军事意象。

branches.en: Subsidy, grant, and support all answer a shortage from behind.
branches.cn: 补贴、补助与支持，都是从后方回应短缺。

intro.en: Subsidy is built on the Latin noun subsidium, with English words for paying, receiving, and the act of support.
intro.cn: subsidy 建立在拉丁语名词 subsidium 之上，英语围绕它构成支付、受助与支援行为等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin subsidium means reserve troops or help, from sub, behind, and sedere, to sit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 subsidium 意为后备队或援助，来自 sub（在后）与 sedere（坐）。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the troops behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把军队安置在后。

items.example: Sedere gives the image of sitting in reserve.

Subsidized describes a supported buyer or seller.

definition_zh: 底土、心土；表土之下的土层
definition_en: the layer of soil below the topsoil, usually poorer in organic matter and richer in clay or gravel
core_image: 坑壁上半是黑土，下半是紧实的黄褐色黏土，锹刃卡在交界处
scene: 挖到一半时，铁锹在深色表土之下碰到了紧实的黄褐色土，铲刃一滑，工人说 This subsoil is stiff clay that water can hardly pass through.
sceneCN: 这里 subsoil 指「表土之下的那层土」，取第 1 个义项（层位本身）；句意为这层底土是紧实的黏土，水几乎渗不过去。图中可辨识物件：坑壁、深色表土、黄褐黏土、铁锹。

pos.zh: 底土、心土（多作不可数，指具体土类时可用复数 subsoils）

derivatives.zh: 各类底土（复数，调查用语）
深松作业；不翻乱土层的深层松土

senses.title: The layer under the surface soil
senses.definition: the soil layer lying immediately below the topsoil, lower in organic matter and usually denser
senses.definitionCN: 紧接表土之下、有机质更少且通常更紧实的土层
senses.example: Roots stopped where the subsoil turned stony.
senses.exampleCN: 根在底土变多石的地方就停住了。
senses.why: The Latin prefix sub- means under, so the word simply places a soil layer beneath the one named first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 sub- 意为「在下」，因此这个词只是把一层土放在先说到的那层之下。

senses.title: Clay-enriched subsoil
senses.definition: the layer where clay washed down from above has collected, forming a dense band
senses.definitionCN: 从上方淋洗下来的黏土在此聚集、形成紧实条带的那一层
senses.example: The red subsoil holds so much clay that it cracks in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 红色底土含黏土太多，夏天会开裂。
senses.why: Fine clay particles move downward with water until they stick, so the densest band forms below the leached zone.
senses.whyCN: 细小黏粒随水下移直到附着，因此最紧实的那条带形成于淋溶层之下。

senses.title: A mineral layer with little life
senses.definition: the part of the profile where roots, worms and organic matter are scarce
senses.definitionCN: 剖面上根系、蚯蚓与有机质都很少的那部分
senses.example: Few earthworms reach the subsoil except along old root channels.
senses.exampleCN: 除了沿着旧根孔，很少有蚯蚓到达底土。
senses.why: Fresh organic matter is added at the surface, so life thins out with depth and the layer stays mineral.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜有机质只在地表加入，因此生命随深度变稀，这一层始终保持矿质状态。

senses.title: Bearing layer for foundations
senses.definition: the firm layer engineers rely on to carry the weight of a structure
senses.definitionCN: 工程师依靠来承受建筑物重量的紧实土层
senses.example: The footings were taken down to the firm subsoil.
senses.exampleCN: 基础一直做到坚硬的底土层。
senses.why: Loose surface soil settles, so loads are transferred to the denser layer below it.
senses.whyCN: 松散的表土会沉降，因此荷载被传到它下面更紧实的层。

senses.title: A barrier to roots and water
senses.titleCN: 限制根系与水分的紧实层
senses.definition: a compacted or clay-rich band that stops roots and slows drainage
senses.definitionCN: 压实或富黏土的条带，阻止根系下扎并减慢排水
senses.example: A hard subsoil kept the orchard waterlogged all spring.
senses.exampleCN: 紧实的底土让果园整个春天都积水。
senses.why: Water fills the pores above a dense layer and cannot drain, which is why farmers deep-loosen such subsoil.
senses.whyCN: 水在紧实层之上的孔隙里积满而排不出去，因此农民要对这种底土做深松。

senses.title: Layers below the topsoil in a trench
senses.titleCN: 探坑中表土以下的沉积
senses.definition: the sediment or buried soil beneath the modern surface, read in excavations
senses.definitionCN: 现代地表之下的沉积物或埋藏土，在发掘中读取
senses.example: The trench showed a buried subsoil under the modern fill.
senses.exampleCN: 探沟显示现代填土之下有一层埋藏底土。
senses.why: Excavation uses the word for any layer under the present surface, even when it is no longer soil in the farming sense.
senses.whyCN: 考古发掘把这个词用于现今地表之下的任何一层，即使它已不是农业意义上的土壤。

senses.title: Material dug for fill
senses.definition: subsoil removed and used as bulk fill on another site
senses.definitionCN: 被挖出并用于别处作为大体量填方的底土
senses.example: Trucks carried the subsoil to the embankment works.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车把底土运到路堤工地。
senses.why: Because the layer is abundant, cheap and stony, it is quarried for fill rather than saved for growing.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一层量大、便宜又多石，它常被采作填方，而不是留作种植。

senses.title: Contrast with topsoil and parent material
senses.definition: the middle term in the standard three-part division of the profile
senses.definitionCN: 剖面标准三分法中居中的那一项
senses.example: Descriptions separate topsoil, subsoil and parent material before naming the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 描述时先区分表土、底土与母质，再给土壤命名。
senses.why: Field survey needed three simple terms, and subsoil was the neutral middle one that is neither worked nor unweathered.
senses.whyCN: 野外调查需要三个简单术语，而底土正是既不耕作、也未风化的那个中性中间项。

intro.en: Subsoil is Latin sub-, under, welded to the English noun soil, which itself came from Old French and Latin solum. The compound belongs to nineteenth-century agricultural writing.
intro.cn: subsoil 是拉丁前缀 sub-「在下」加英语名词 soil 构成，而 soil 本身来自古法语与拉丁 solum。这个复合词属于十九世纪的农业文献。

items.en: Sub- meant under or below in Latin and appears in dozens of English words such as submarine and subsoil.
items.cn: sub- 在拉丁语中意为「在下、低于」，出现在 submarine、subsoil 等大量英语词中。

items.en: Solum meant ground, floor or sole, and it reached English as soil through Old French.
items.cn: solum 意为地面、地板或脚底，经古法语以 soil 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writers paired subsoil with topsoil to describe the depth that the plough did not reach.
items.cn: 十九世纪作者把 subsoil 与 topsoil 配对使用，用来描述犁所达不到的深度。

items.en: In the twentieth century the same word covered bearing layers under foundations and bulk fill dug from below the surface.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，同一个词又涵盖基础下的持力层，以及从地表以下挖出的大体量填方。

items.en: The verb to subsoil, meaning to loosen deep layers without turning them up, is a back-formation from the noun.
items.cn: 动词 subsoil 意为深松而不把下层翻上来，是由名词逆构而来。

note.en: Group one holds layer terms whose positions are easy to confuse; group two holds materials that resemble subsoil in use.
note.cn: 第一组是位置容易混淆的层位词；第二组是用途上与底土相似的材料。

entries.definition: The fertile dark layer at the surface, the direct opposite in position and usually in quality.
entries.definitionCN: 地表那层肥沃深色的土，在位置与质量上通常都与之相对。

entries.definition: The rock or sediment from which the soil formed, lying beneath the subsoil or forming its lower limit.
entries.definitionCN: 形成土壤的岩石或沉积物，位于底土之下或构成其下限。

entries.definition: Any underlying material or surface; it is used in biology and engineering rather than soil survey.
entries.definitionCN: 任何底层材料或表面；用于生物学与工程，而非土壤调查。

entries.definition: The prepared soil surface under a road or pavement, which may be natural subsoil or imported fill.
entries.definitionCN: 道路或铺面之下经过处理的土面，可能是天然底土，也可能是外运填方。

entries.definition: A very dense layer cemented by clay, iron or calcium carbonate that roots and water cannot pass.
entries.definitionCN: 由黏土、铁或碳酸钙胶结成的极紧实层，根系与水都无法通过。

entries.definition: A dense clay-rich horizon inside the subsoil; it is a kind of subsoil rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 底土内部的富黏土紧实层；它是底土的一种，而不是同义词。

entries.definition: All material above a seam, including topsoil and subsoil; the word is defined by the seam, not by soil layers.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在矿层之上的全部材料，包含表土与底土；该词以矿层定义，而非以土层定义。

entries.definition: Material deliberately put in place to raise ground; subsoil becomes fill only after it is dug and moved.
entries.definitionCN: 为抬高地面而特意填入的材料；底土只有被挖出搬运后才成为填方。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prefix, the real topsoil pair and the real engineering uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀、真实的表土配对与真实的工程用法。

normal.en: Sub- means under, so subsoil is simply the under-soil.
normal.cn: sub- 意为在下，因此 subsoil 就是「下面的土」。

normal.en: Topsoil is dark and full of roots; subsoil is pale, dense and stony.
normal.cn: 表土深色多根；底土浅色、紧实、多石。

normal.en: Three-part profile: topsoil, subsoil, parent material.
normal.cn: 剖面三分：表土、底土、母质。

normal.en: A dense subsoil causes waterlogging, which is why farmers deep-loosen it.
normal.cn: 紧实的底土会造成积水，因此农民要深松它。

normal.en: Engineers look for subsoil when they need a firm bearing layer.
normal.cn: 工程师需要坚实地基时找的就是底土。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge on top of a brick: water passes the sponge and stops at the brick.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵压在砖上：水穿过海绵，到砖就停住了。

abstract.en: Picture a layer that holds up a building while nothing lives in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一层土撑着整栋楼，里面却没有任何生命。

abstract.en: Picture clay that cracks into deep plates in a dry summer.
abstract.cn: 想象干旱的夏天黏土裂成一块块深板。

examples.en: The subsoil here is heavy clay with very little air.
examples.cn: 这里的底土是几乎不含空气的重黏土。

examples.en: Water sat on the field because the subsoil drained poorly.
examples.cn: 水积在田里，因为底土排水很差。

examples.en: Engineers tested the subsoil before choosing the foundation type.
examples.cn: 工程师先检测底土，再决定基础类型。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从这一层本身走到黏土带、缺乏生命、基础持力、阻水阻根、探沟中的用法、作填方，以及三分法中的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spade striking stiff clay just under the dark surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁锹在深色表层之下碰到紧实的黏土。

branches.en: POSITION: the middle term between topsoil and parent material.
branches.cn: 位置：介于表土与母质之间的中间项。

branches.en: COMPOSITION: clay washed down, and life left behind.
branches.cn: 组成：黏土淋洗下来，生命被留在上面。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: strong enough to carry a building, dense enough to stop water.

intro.en: Subsoil is the Latin prefix sub- plus the noun soil, and the prefix recurs in a large family of English words.

definition_zh: 亚种；种以下的分类等级
definition_en: a group of populations within a species that differ from other populations, usually in geography or form
core_image: 同一片大陆上被山脉隔开的两群同类，毛色深浅不同，却仍能互交
scene: 博物馆把来自两座相隔很远的岛屿的甲虫标本定为同一物种下的两个不同亚种。 The museum assigned beetle specimens from two distant islands to two different subspecies of the same species.
sceneCN: 这里 subspecies 是「亚种」（第 1 个义项：种之下的分类等级）；句意：博物馆把来自两座相隔很远岛屿的甲虫标本，定为同一物种下的两个不同亚种。

pos.zh: 亚种（单复数同形，略作 subsp. 或 ssp.）

derivatives.zh: 变种（植物分类中低于亚种的等级）
变型（植物分类中的最低等级）

senses.title: A rank below species
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank immediately below species, grouping populations that share a distinct set of features
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在物种之下的分类阶元，把具有一组独特性状的群体聚合起来
senses.example: The museum assigned the two island beetles to different subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把两座岛上的甲虫定为不同的亚种。
senses.why: Sub- 'under' plus species makes the rank literal: the same kind, divided one step further down.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下」加 species 把阶元关系写得很直白：同一个种，再往下分一级。

senses.title: A geographical race
senses.definition: a set of populations separated by geography that have come to differ in colour, size or behaviour while remaining interfertile
senses.definitionCN: 因地理分隔而在毛色、体型或行为上出现差异、却仍能互交的群体
senses.example: The northern subspecies is darker and slightly smaller.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的亚种颜色更深，体型略小。
senses.why: Most subspecies begin as geography: a barrier stops gene flow long enough for local features to accumulate, but not long enough to block breeding.
senses.whyCN: 多数亚种起于地理：屏障阻断基因流的时间足以让地方特征积累，却还不足以阻断繁殖。

senses.title: The trinomial name
senses.definition: the three-part scientific name that adds a subspecies epithet to the binomial, as in Homo sapiens sapiens
senses.definitionCN: 在双名之后再加一个亚种加词的三段式学名，如智人的指名亚种
senses.example: The trinomial name repeats the species epithet for the nominate subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 指名亚种的名称会把种加词重复一遍。
senses.why: Because a subspecies sits below a species, its name needs one more slot; the trinomial is that slot, and it is written in italics with the rank not capitalized.
senses.whyCN: 由于亚种位于种之下，其名称需要多一个位置；三名法就是那个位置，书写时用斜体且亚种加词不大写。

senses.title: Nomenclatural rules and abbreviations
senses.definition: the set of rules that govern valid subspecies names, together with the abbreviations subsp. and ssp. used in catalogs
senses.definitionCN: 管理亚种名称有效性的规则，以及标本目录中使用的缩写 subsp. 与 ssp.
senses.example: The label reads subsp. borealis, following the code.
senses.exampleCN: 标签按法规写作 subsp. borealis。
senses.why: Codes exist so that a name means the same thing in every collection; the abbreviation marks the rank without spelling it out, which saves space on a label.
senses.whyCN: 法规的存在是为了让一个名称在每一份收藏中都指同一事物；缩写在不写出全称的情况下标出阶元，可节省标签空间。

senses.title: Plural identical to singular
senses.definition: the form subspecies used for both one and several, following the Latin pattern of species
senses.definitionCN: 一个与多个都写作 subspecies，沿用 species 的拉丁模式
senses.example: Two subspecies were recognized, and one subspecies was newly described.
senses.exampleCN: 识别出两个亚种，其中一个为新描述。
senses.why: Latin species had an unchanging plural, and the compound keeps it: only the verb or a numeral shows whether the word is singular.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 species 的复数不变，这个复合词沿用了这一点：只有动词或数词能表明该词是单数还是复数。

senses.title: Subspecies and variety in botany
senses.titleCN: 植物学中亚种与变种的分别
senses.definition: in botanical nomenclature, a rank that ranks above variety and below species, used for geographically distinct wild populations
senses.definitionCN: 植物命名法中位于变种之上、物种之下、用于地理上独立的野生群体的等级
senses.example: Botanists treat the coastal form as a subspecies, not a variety.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把海岸类型处理为亚种，而不是变种。
senses.why: Botany needed finer steps than zoology, so it placed variety and forma below subspecies; the two words are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要比动物学更细的台阶，于是在亚种之下再设变种与变型；这两个词不能互换。

senses.title: A unit in conservation planning
senses.definition: a population unit recognized in conservation because its distinct traits would be lost if it disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 因其独特性状一旦消失就会丧失、而在保护工作中被承认的群体单元
senses.example: Managers list the island subspecies as a priority for captive breeding.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者把这个岛屿亚种列为圈养繁殖的优先对象。
senses.why: Conservation works with units it can act on; a named subspecies gives a legal and practical handle even when the biological status is debated.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要可施加行动的单元；即使生物学地位仍有争议，一个有名称的亚种也提供了法律与实践上的抓手。

senses.title: Subspecies in microbiology
senses.definition: a formal rank used for bacterial strains that differ in antigenic or biochemical characters within one species
senses.definitionCN: 用于同一物种内抗原或生化性状不同的菌株的正式等级
senses.example: The culture was classified as a subspecies of the common gut bacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 该培养物被定为常见肠道细菌的一个亚种。
senses.why: Microbiology adopted the rank because bacterial species can be very broad; subspecies gives a legal name to a recognizable strain without raising it to species.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学采用这个等级，因为细菌的种可以定得很宽；亚种给了可辨识菌株一个正式名称，而无需把它提升为种。

senses.title: The rank as a matter of judgement
senses.titleCN: 作为判断问题的亚种划分
senses.definition: a classification that depends on how much difference taxonomists decide is enough, and therefore often revised
senses.definitionCN: 取决于分类学家认定差异足够大与否、因而常被修订的分类处理
senses.example: The two subspecies were later merged when the boundary proved continuous.
senses.exampleCN: 当界线被证明是连续的，这两个亚种后来被合并。
senses.why: Subspecies is the rank most exposed to disagreement, since the line between a local form and a full species is drawn by judgement rather than by a single test.
senses.whyCN: 亚种是最容易引起分歧的阶元，因为地方类型与完整物种之间的界线靠判断划定，而不是靠单一判据。

intro.en: Subspecies is a modern scientific compound: Latin sub- 'under' fastened to species. It was coined for taxonomy rather than inherited from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subspecies 是近代科学复合词：拉丁前缀 sub-「在下」加 species，为分类学而造，并非从拉丁语整体继承。年代为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below' and was already productive in Latin compounds such as subicere and substructio.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，在拉丁复合词中已很能产，如 subicere 与 substructio。

items.en: Species meant 'appearance, kind' and served as the basic logical class before it became a biological rank.
items.cn: species 意为「外观、种类」，在成为生物阶元之前是基本的逻辑类别。

items.en: As ranks multiplied, naturalists needed a step between the broad species of the day and the local form, and the compound was available.
items.cn: 随着阶元增多，博物学者需要在当时较宽的种与地方类型之间加一级，而这个复合形式正好可用。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century nomenclature codes fixed the trinomial and the abbreviations subsp. and ssp.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的命名法规确定了三名法以及 subsp.、ssp. 两种缩写。

items.en: Molecular data have forced many subspecies to be merged or raised, so the rank is now more often a provisional judgement than a settled fact.
items.cn: 分子数据迫使许多亚种被合并或提升，因此这个阶元如今更像临时判断，而非定论。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of subspecies as a formal rank is not fixed here, and no classical Latin noun subspecies is attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：subspecies 作为正式阶元的最早使用年份此处无法确定；古典拉丁语中并无 subspecies 这一名词。

note.en: Group one separates ranks and names that sit near subspecies; group two compares the words for local forms at different depths.
note.cn: 第一组区分与亚种相邻的阶元与名称；第二组比较不同深度的「地方类型」用词。

entries.definition: The basic rank itself: one step up from subspecies, and the unit that the trinomial's second word names.
entries.definitionCN: 基本阶元本身：比亚种高一级，也是三名法中第二个词所命名的单位。

entries.definition: Relating to a subspecies, as in subspecific epithet. It is the adjective, while subspecies is the rank noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与亚种有关的，如亚种加词。它是形容词，subspecies 是阶元名词。

entries.definition: A group of closely related species treated together, the opposite direction from subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干近缘物种合并看待的类群，方向与亚种相反。

entries.definition: A mathematical space contained in another space. Sub- is shared, but species is not the source; it is built on space.
entries.definitionCN: 包含于另一空间的数学空间。共用了 sub-，但词源不是 species，而是建立在 space 之上。

entries.definition: In botany, a rank below subspecies for a minor wild variant; in everyday use, simply a sort or kind.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中位于亚种之下、用于细微野生变异的等级；日常则泛指种类。

entries.definition: A loosely used term for a geographically distinct breeding group; it has no fixed rank in the codes.
entries.definitionCN: 对地理上独立的繁殖群体的宽松称呼；在命名法规中没有固定阶元。

entries.definition: A genetically distinct line maintained in the laboratory or in breeding, finer and less formal than a subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 实验室或育种中保持的遗传独立品系，比亚种更细、更不正式。

entries.definition: In botany, forma, a minor morphological variant below variety; the smallest recognized step.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中的变型，位于变种之下、最小的可识别台阶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub- 'under' plus species: one step below the basic rank.
normal.cn: sub-「在下」加 species：基本阶元之下的一级。

normal.en: The trinomial adds a third word: genus, species, subspecies.
normal.cn: 三名法再加一个词：属名、种名、亚种名。

normal.en: The nomination subspecies repeats the species epithet, which makes it easy to spot in a name.
normal.cn: 指名亚种会重复种加词，因此在名称里一眼可辨。

normal.en: Botany puts variety and forma below subspecies, so the ranks are ordered rather than interchangeable.
normal.cn: 植物学把变种与变型放在亚种之下，因此这些阶元有先后，不能互换。

normal.en: Labels abbreviate the rank as subsp. or ssp. to save space.
normal.cn: 标签把阶元缩写成 subsp. 或 ssp. 以节省空间。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a map by a committee, revised at the next meeting.

examples.en: A recent review sank three subspecies into one on genetic evidence.
examples.cn: 最近一篇综述依据遗传证据把三个亚种合并为一个。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of subspecies follow the rank from its formal position downward: a step below species, a geographic race, a three-word name, a set of naming rules, an unchanging plural, a botanical neighbour, a conservation unit, a microbiological label and finally a judgement that keeps being revised.
sensesIntro.cn: subspecies 的九个义项沿着这个阶元向下展开：种下的一级、地理宗、三名式名称、命名规则、不变的复数、植物学中的邻级、保护单元、微生物学标签，最后是一个不断被修订的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind divided by a map line that is real enough to name but not deep enough to split.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个种类被一条地图上的线分开，足以命名，却不足以分裂。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS ORIGIN: a step below species, usually produced by geography.
branches.cn: 阶元与来源：种下的一级，通常由地理分隔产生。

branches.en: THE NAME: three words, a code of rules, and a plural that never changes form.
branches.cn: 名称：三个词、一套规则、一个永不改变形式的复数。

branches.en: BOTANICAL ORDER: variety and forma sit still lower, so the ranks form a ladder.
branches.cn: 植物学的次序：变种与变型还在更低处，阶元因此形成梯子。

branches.en: APPLIED USES: conservation acts on the named unit, microbiology uses it for strains.
branches.cn: 应用：保护工作作用于有名称的单元，微生物学用它标记菌株。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: how much difference is enough is decided, not measured.
branches.cn: 判断：差异要多大才算够，是决定的，不是测出来的。

intro.en: Subspecies is built from two Latin pieces but is itself a modern scientific word; the pieces are transparent even though the compound is recent.
intro.cn: subspecies 由两个拉丁成分构成，但本身是近代科学词；复合词虽新，成分却透明。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sub- 衍生 submarine、subsoil、subordinate；species 衍生 species、subspecies、speciation。

definition_en: the act of putting one person or thing in the place of another
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被另一枚同色棋子换下，方格上的位置标记保持不变

pos.zh: 替换；代替；代换；（数学）代入；（化学）取代；（体育）换人（指行为时可数，指过程或概念时多不可数）

senses.title: Putting one thing in another's place
senses.titleCN: 替换行为：以他物占据其位
senses.definition: the act of using one person or thing in place of another
senses.definitionCN: 用一个人或物代替另一个的行为
senses.example: The substitution of fresh herbs for dried ones changed the dish.
senses.exampleCN: 用新鲜香草代替干香草改变了这道菜。
senses.why: Latin substituere meant 'to set one thing under or in place of another'; the noun names that placing, not the thing placed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 substituere 意为「把一物置于另一物之下或其位」，名词命名这一放置动作，而不是被放置之物。

senses.title: Substitution into an equation
senses.titleCN: 数学代入：把值放进变量的位置
senses.definition: in algebra, the replacement of a variable by a number or expression
senses.definitionCN: 在代数中用数值或表达式替换变量
senses.example: Substitution of x = 3 gives the value of the expression.
senses.exampleCN: 代入 x = 3 即可得到该表达式的值。
senses.why: Mathematics adopted the word for the mechanical act of putting a value where a symbol stood, which is the literal Latin image of placing one thing in another's position.
senses.whyCN: 数学采用该词表示把数值放到符号原先所在位置的机械动作，这正是拉丁语「置一物于其位」的字面意象。

senses.title: A chemical substitution reaction
senses.titleCN: 化学取代：基团被另一基团换下
senses.definition: a reaction in which one atom or group in a molecule is replaced by another
senses.definitionCN: 分子中一个原子或基团被另一个所替换的反应
senses.example: Nucleophilic substitution replaces the bromide with a hydroxyl group.
senses.exampleCN: 亲核取代用羟基替换溴离子。
senses.why: Chemists keep the word because a group literally leaves and another takes its site on the carbon skeleton, so the Latin idea of placing in position fits the mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 化学家沿用该词，是因为一个基团确实离开，另一个占据它在碳骨架上的位置，拉丁语「置于其位」的思路正好契合这一机理。

senses.title: A player sent on for another
senses.titleCN: 体育换人：替补球员换下场上球员
senses.definition: in team sports, the replacement of one player by another during a match
senses.definitionCN: 团队运动中在比赛进行时用一名球员换下另一名
senses.example: The coach made a substitution at halftime to strengthen the midfield.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在半场换人，以加强中场。
senses.why: Sport borrows the general act and makes it a counted event: a team has a limited number of substitutions, so the noun names both the act and the slot used.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了这一一般动作，并把它变成可计数的赛事事件：球队的换人次数有限，因此名词既指动作，也指用掉的那个名额。

senses.title: The substitution effect in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学替代效应：转向更便宜的替代品
senses.definition: the change in demand caused by a consumer switching to a cheaper alternative when a price rises
senses.definitionCN: 价格上涨时消费者转向更便宜替代品所引起的需求变化
senses.example: The substitution effect explains why sales of the cheaper brand rose.
senses.exampleCN: 替代效应解释了为什么较便宜品牌的销量上升。
senses.why: Economics turns the act into a named force: one good takes the place of another in the buyer's basket, and the effect is measured separately from income.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把这一动作变成有名称的力量：一种商品在买家的篮子里取代另一种，这一效应与收入效应分开计量。

senses.title: Substitution in language teaching
senses.titleCN: 语言学替换：同一位置上换形式
senses.definition: in linguistics and language teaching, the replacement of one form by another in the same slot, as in a substitution drill
senses.definitionCN: 语言学与语言教学中，用另一形式替换同一位置上的形式，如替换练习
senses.example: The substitution drill swaps one noun for another in the same frame.
senses.exampleCN: 替换练习在同一句型框架内用一个名词换掉另一个。
senses.why: A substitution class is a set of forms that can occupy the same position; the term names the test that identifies the slot.
senses.whyCN: 替换类指能占据同一位置的一组形式；这个术语命名识别该位置的测试。

senses.title: A substitution cipher
senses.titleCN: 密码替换：按规则逐符号替换
senses.definition: a cipher in which each symbol or letter is replaced by another according to a fixed rule
senses.definitionCN: 按固定规则把每个符号或字母替换成另一个的密码
senses.example: A simple substitution cipher is easy to break by counting letter frequencies.
senses.exampleCN: 简单的替换密码很容易通过统计字母频率破解。
senses.why: The cipher is named for the operation, not the key: every unit is systematically replaced, which is the plain sense of substitutio applied to symbols.
senses.whyCN: 这种密码因操作而得名，而非因密钥：每个单元被系统性地替换，这正是 substitutio 用于符号时的字面义。

senses.title: Replacing a party to a contract
senses.titleCN: 合同主体替换：换人而不换义务
senses.definition: in law, the replacement of one party, debtor or obligation by another, often with the consent of the remaining party
senses.definitionCN: 法律中用另一方替换合同一方、债务人或者义务，通常需剩余一方同意
senses.example: The lender agreed to the substitution of a new guarantor.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款方同意更换新的担保人。
senses.why: Contract law needs a precise word for a change of person rather than of terms; substitution marks that the obligation continues while the party occupying it changes.
senses.whyCN: 合同法需要一个精确的词来表示「换人而非换条款」；substitution 标记义务延续、占据该义务的主体发生变更。

intro.en: Substitution comes from Latin substitutio, the action noun of substituere 'to set in place of another', from sub- 'under, instead of' plus statuere 'to set, make stand', which itself comes from stare 'to stand'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: substitution 出自拉丁 substitutio，即 substituere「使替代、置于其位」的动作名词；substituere 由 sub-「在下、代替」与 statuere「安置、使站立」构成，而 statuere 又出自 stare「站立」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin statuere 'to set up, place, establish' comes from stare 'to stand' and supplies the idea of setting something in a position.
items.cn: 拉丁 statuere「竖立、安置、确立」出自 stare「站立」，提供「把某物放到某个位置」的思路。

items.en: substituere, from sub- 'under, in place of' plus statuere, meant 'to set in place of another, put under'.
items.cn: substituere 由 sub-「在下、代替」与 statuere 构成，意为「把一物置于另一物之位、置于其下」。

items.en: substitutio is the action noun of substituere, formed with -io; it names the act of setting one thing in another's place.
items.cn: substitutio 是 substituere 的动作名词，以 -io 构成，命名「把一物置于另一物之位」的动作。

items.en: Old French substitution and Latin substitutio supply the English noun in the fifteenth century; substitute appears first as a person and later as a verb.
items.cn: 古法语 substitution 与拉丁 substitutio 于十五世纪提供英语名词；substitute 先指人，后作动词。

items.en: Algebra, chemistry and team sport each took the word between the eighteenth and twentieth centuries because each turns a symbol, a group or a player into a replaceable slot.
items.cn: 代数、化学与团队运动在十八至二十世纪各自采用该词，因为它们都把符号、基团或球员变成可替换的位置。

items.en: The first English citation of substitution is uncertain. Latin sub- has several shades, 'under' and 'instead of' among them, and which shade is primary in substituere is a matter of interpretation rather than record; the Indo-European root of stare is reconstructed as *steh₂-.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：substitution 的英语最早书证年代不明。拉丁 sub- 有数种含义，「在下」与「代替」都在其中，substituere 中哪一义为主属解释问题而非文献记录；stare 的印欧词根被重构为 *steh₂-。

note.en: The first group separates the substitute family by part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms, with register and direction of change as the main differences.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 substitute 词族；第二组给出近义词，主要差别在语域与替换的方向性。

entries.definition: The stand-in or the act of standing in; substitution is the abstract noun for that act.
entries.definitionCN: 指替代者，或指代替的动作；substitution 是表示该动作的抽象名词。

entries.definition: Relating to substitution, common in legal and religious language; it modifies a noun rather than naming the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为与替换有关的，常见于法律与宗教语言；它修饰名词，而不是命名动作。

entries.definition: Capable of being replaced; it describes a property of the thing, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 意为可被替代的；它描述事物的属性，而不是事件。

entries.definition: Serving as a substitute; it describes the role something plays, not the act of change.
entries.definitionCN: 意为起替代作用的；它描述某物所扮演的角色，而不是替换动作。

entries.definition: The everyday word for putting a new thing in place, often permanently; substitution is more formal and technical, and is the usual term in maths, chemistry and sport.
entries.definitionCN: 指把新物放到原位的日常说法，常含永久替换之意；substitution 更正式、更技术化，是数学、化学与体育中的常用术语。

entries.definition: A casual exchange, often of two things traded for each other; substitution is one-directional and neutral in register.
entries.definitionCN: 指随意的交换，常为两物互换；substitution 是单向的，语域中性偏正式。

entries.definition: Giving one thing and receiving another; substitution need not involve anything coming back.
entries.definitionCN: 指给出一物并收到另一物；substitution 不一定涉及回返之物。

entries.definition: A person or thing acting in another's role, especially in medicine or law; it names the stand-in, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指代替他人角色的对象，尤用于医学或法律；它命名替代者，而不是替换行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub- (in place of) + stitut (set, from statuere) + -ion: setting one thing in another's place.
normal.cn: sub-（代替）+ stitut（安置，出自 statuere）+ -ion：把一物置于另一物之位。

normal.en: The family runs substitute, substitution, substitutable, substitutional, substitutive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 substitute、substitution、substitutable、substitutional、substitutive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: substitution effect, substitution cipher, nucleophilic substitution, make a substitution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各领域：替代效应、替换密码、亲核取代、进行换人。

normal.en: A substitute is the stand-in; substitution is the change; substitutable is the property.
normal.cn: substitute 是替代者，substitution 是替换，substitutable 是可替代的性质。

normal.en: Replacement is plain and often permanent; substitution is formal, technical and slot-based.
normal.cn: replacement 平实且常指永久替换；substitution 正式、技术化，并以「位置」为核心。

examples.en: A substitution cipher hides the message by replacing each letter.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one act, putting one thing in another's place: plain replacement, substitution into an equation, a group taking a site in a molecule, a player coming on, the substitution effect, a language slot, a cipher alphabet and a change of contract party.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一动作「把一物置于另一物之位」：一般替换、数学代入、化学基团顶替、球员上场、替代效应、语言位置、密码字母表，以及合同主体变更。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one piece is lifted and another set down on the same square.

branches.en: PLAIN AND CODED: one object or symbol takes another's place.

branches.cn: 形式系统：数值进入方程，基团占据分子上的位点。

senses.title: The arithmetic operation
senses.definition: the operation of taking one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数里拿走另一个数的运算
senses.example: Subtraction is taught alongside addition in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 减法在一年级就与加法一起教。
senses.why: The noun names the operation itself, built directly on the Latin verb for drawing away.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接由拉丁动词「抽走」构成，指运算本身。

senses.title: The working of such a problem
senses.definition: the written or mental working by which such a problem is solved
senses.definitionCN: 解这类题时写出来或心算的过程
senses.example: Her subtraction was neat, with every borrow marked.
senses.exampleCN: 她的减法写得整齐，每次借位都标了出来。
senses.why: English lets the name of the operation also cover the steps taken to carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 英语让运算的名称同时覆盖执行它的步骤。

senses.title: The amount taken away
senses.definition: the quantity that is removed from a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 从较大量中取走的那份量
senses.example: The subtraction from the budget was larger than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 预算被削减的数额比预期更大。
senses.why: The same noun serves for the act and for its result, a pattern English uses constantly.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指动作也指结果，这是英语常见的做法。

senses.title: A reduction in amount
senses.definition: a decrease in an amount, especially one made deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 数量的减少，尤指有意造成的减少
senses.example: A subtraction of ten staff changed the office entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 减掉十名员工让办公室完全变了样。
senses.why: Counting the removed part turns naturally into naming the reduction itself.
senses.whyCN: 为被拿走的部分计数，自然就转为命名这次减少。

senses.title: The minus sign in notation
senses.definition: the sign used to mark this operation in written arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 书面算术中标记这一运算的符号
senses.example: A subtraction sign is a short horizontal stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 减号是一道短短的横线。
senses.why: The sign is called by the name of the operation it performs, a common shorthand in mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号以它所执行的运算命名，是数学里常见的简写。

senses.title: A deduction in accounts
senses.definition: an item deducted before a balance is struck
senses.definitionCN: 结账之前被扣除的项目
senses.example: The statement lists each subtraction from the gross sum.
senses.exampleCN: 账单把从总额中扣掉的每一项都列了出来。
senses.why: Bookkeeping treats every removal as a named entry, so the operation becomes a line in a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 记账把每次移除都当成一个有名字的条目，于是运算变成账簿上的一行。

senses.title: Finding what remains by exclusion
senses.definition: the method of finding what is left by ruling out what it is not
senses.definitionCN: 通过排除「不是什么」来求出剩下的是什么
senses.example: The detective worked by subtraction, discarding every impossible route.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探用排除法，把每条不可能的路都划掉。
senses.why: The metaphor extends the arithmetic: whatever is ruled out is taken away until one answer remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把算术延伸开：凡被排除的都被拿走，直到只剩一个答案。

senses.title: Stripping away the unnecessary
senses.definition: the act of removing whatever is not essential
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一切非必要成分的行为
senses.example: The final edit was pure subtraction, cutting every line that repeated the point.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一轮修改纯粹是做减法，删掉了每一句重复的话。
senses.why: With numbers gone, subtraction becomes the discipline of taking away rather than the count of what is left.
senses.whyCN: 数字消失之后，减法变成「取走」的自律，而不是对剩余之物的计数。

intro.en: Subtraction comes from Late Latin subtractio, a noun of action from subtrahere 'to draw away'. The verb is sub- 'from below' plus trahere 'to draw'; the earlier origin of trahere is unsettled.
intro.cn: subtraction 出自晚期拉丁名词 subtractio，是 subtrahere「抽走」的动作名词；该动词由 sub-「从下面」加 trahere「拉」构成，trahere 的更早来源无定论。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, pull'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, so any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」。它在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其引出的更古老形式都属重构形式。

items.en: Sub- 'from below' plus trahere gave subtrahere 'to draw away, take away'.
items.cn: sub-「从下面」加 trahere 得出 subtrahere「抽走、拿走」。

items.en: The action noun subtractio named the drawing away itself; English took the noun rather than the Latin verb form.
items.cn: 动作名词 subtractio 指「抽走」这件事本身；英语取的是这个名词，而非拉丁动词原形。

items.en: The noun appeared in English in the fifteenth century, at first in general use and only later as a school term.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪进入英语，起初是一般用法，后来才成为课堂术语。

items.en: Printing and schooling fixed subtraction as the standard name of the operation from the seventeenth century onward.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，印刷与学校教育使 subtraction 固定为这项运算的标准名称。

items.en: The figurative sense of ruling things out till one answer remains is modern and rests on the arithmetic image.
items.cn: 「不断排除直到只剩一个答案」的比喻用法属现代发展，依托于算术形象。

note.en: Group one holds words that wear the same noun ending or come from the same verb; group two holds words for a decrease or a deduction.
note.cn: 第一组是共用同一名词词尾、或出自同一动词的词；第二组是表示「减少」或「扣除」的近义词。

entries.definition: The inverse operation, built on a different Latin verb; the matching ending hides a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 与之相反的运算，出自另一个拉丁动词；相同的词尾掩盖了不同的词根。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed; the noun names the operation, the verb the act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词由这个动词构成；名词指运算，动词指动作。

entries.definition: The technical name for the quantity taken away, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 被取走那个量的专门名称，出自同一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From de- plus ducere 'lead': a leading away, hence an amount deducted; the ending matches but the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de- 加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引走」，引申为扣除额；词尾相同而词根不同。

entries.definition: A general word for making an amount smaller, whether by taking away or by lowering a rate.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量变小的通称，无论靠拿走一部分还是靠降低比率。

entries.definition: To become or make less, used of sizes, rates and numbers without any arithmetic frame.
entries.definitionCN: 变小或使变小，用于尺寸、比率与数量，不带算术框架。

entries.definition: The act of moving something out of its place, usually physical.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移出原位的动作，通常指实物。

entries.definition: An informal word for a reduction ordered by someone, as in a cut in funding.
entries.definitionCN: 由某方决定削减的口语说法，如削减经费。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is the verb plus an action ending, so it names the operation rather than the person doing it.
normal.cn: 名词由动词加动作词尾构成，因此它指运算，而不是做运算的人。

normal.en: The family runs subtract, subtraction, subtractive, subtrahend and subtractional.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：减去、减法、减去的、减数、减法上的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the classroom: a subtraction problem, a subtraction sign, repeated subtraction.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出课堂场景：减法题、减号、连减。

normal.en: Every word built on the same root differs by prefix: away, together, out, apart, from below.
normal.cn: 同根词只靠前缀区别：离开、一起、向外、分开、从下面。

normal.en: In a written sum the removed number is the subtrahend, a Latin tag meaning 'to be subtracted'.
normal.cn: 在竖式里被拿走的那个数是「减数」，这个拉丁标签意为「待减去者」。

abstract.en: Picture a blackboard with one line of figures ruled out and a smaller figure written beneath the rule.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上有一行数字被划掉，横线下面写着一个更小的数。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf from which one book is taken, leaving a gap exactly the size of that book.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上被取走一本书，留下的空当恰好是那本书的大小。

abstract.en: Picture a sculptor's block losing everything that was never part of the figure inside.
abstract.cn: 想象雕刻的石块失去了一切从来不属于里面那个人形的部分。

examples.en: The worksheet mixes addition and subtraction.
examples.cn: 这张练习纸把加法与减法混在一起。

examples.en: Repeated subtraction is one way to introduce division.
examples.cn: 连减是引入除法的一种方式。

examples.en: The subtraction of two senior posts left the team short of experience.
examples.cn: 撤掉两个资深岗位使团队缺少经验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词意为「从底下拉走」，加表示动作或结果的名词词尾，就得到「减法」这件事；被拉走的那份量也用同一个词。

root: 拉丁晚期 subtractio「抽走」＝ sub-（从下面）＋ trahere「拉」，动作名词化；trahere 更早来源无定论。同根动词靠前缀分流：abstract 拉走、contract 拉拢、extract 拉出、distract 拉开。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a part is drawn out of a whole. The operation, its written working, the part removed, the reduction, the sign, the ledger line, the detective's method and the editor's cut are all the same drawing-away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一部分从整体里抽走。运算、竖式过程、被取走的量、数量的减少、运算符号、账上的扣减、侦探的排除法、编者的删削，都是这同一次抽走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rule drawn through one line of figures, leaving a smaller total beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道横线划掉一行数字，线下留下一个更小的总数。

branches.en: THE RULE: the operation and the steps that carry it out share one name.
branches.cn: 规则：运算本身与执行它的步骤共用一个名称。

branches.en: THE PART: what is taken and the resulting reduction are two views of one subtraction.
branches.cn: 部分：被取走的量与由此造成的减少，是同一次减法的两个看法。

branches.en: THE MARK: a short stroke stands for the whole operation.
branches.cn: 标记：一道短横代表整个运算。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: accounts give every removal a line of its own.
branches.cn: 账簿：会计给每一次移除单独列一行。

branches.en: RULING OUT: with no numbers left, subtraction becomes exclusion and then disciplined cutting.
branches.cn: 排除：没有数字之后，减法先变成排除，再变成有纪律的删削。

intro.en: Subtraction is a Latin action noun; its prefix, root and ending each recur across English, so the word repays being read in parts.
intro.cn: subtraction 是一个拉丁动作名词；它的前缀、词根与词尾都在英语中反复出现，因此值得按部分来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin subtrahere yields subtract, subtraction and subtrahend; the ending -io, -ionis becomes English -ion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 subtrahere 衍生 subtract、subtraction 与 subtrahend；词尾 -io、-ionis 在英语中变为 -ion。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀定出取走的方向。

items.example: The Latin verb is the base of the whole family.

definition_zh: 亚热带的；亚热带气候的；副热带的
definition_en: relating to the region or climate just outside the tropics, warm but not fully tropical
core_image: 柑橘树长在山坡上，身后是尚有余热的阳光，前方已吹来温带的风
scene: 山坡上的果园种着柑橘与茶树。Farmers grow citrus and tea in the warm subtropical hills.
sceneCN: 这里 subtropical 指「位于热带外侧、气候温暖的亚热带地区的」（第 1 个义项：紧邻热带但尚未进入热带的纬度地带）；句意为农民在温暖的亚热带山坡上种植柑橘与茶树。图中可辨识物件：梯田果园、柑橘、茶树、远山。

pos.zh: 亚热带的；亚热带气候的

senses.title: Just outside the tropics
senses.titleCN: 亚热带的：紧邻热带外侧的
senses.definition: lying in the belt immediately outside the tropics, usually between about twenty-three and a half and thirty-five degrees of latitude
senses.definitionCN: 位于热带紧邻外侧的地带，通常约在二十三度半到三十五度纬度之间
senses.example: The orchard lies in the subtropical belt north of the Tropic of Cancer.
senses.exampleCN: 这片果园位于北回归线以北的亚热带地带。
senses.why: Sub- 'below, near' plus tropical gives 'nearly tropical'; the belt sits just beyond the turning lines without entering them.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下、靠近」加 tropical 构成「近乎热带」；这条带紧贴折返线之外，但未进入热带。

senses.title: Warm climate with mild winters
senses.titleCN: 亚热带气候的：冬暖夏热的
senses.definition: describing a climate with hot summers and mild, rarely freezing winters
senses.definitionCN: 描述夏热、冬暖且极少结冰的气候
senses.example: Subtropical climates support citrus orchards and winter vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 亚热带气候适合柑橘园与冬季蔬菜。
senses.why: The zone's latitude gives it warm summers and mild winters, so the adjective describes climate as well as position.
senses.whyCN: 这条带的纬度带来暖夏与暖冬，因此形容词既描述位置也描述气候。

senses.title: The subtropical high
senses.titleCN: 副热带高压的：副热带高压带的
senses.definition: relating to the belt of high atmospheric pressure centred near thirty degrees latitude
senses.definitionCN: 与中心位于约三十度纬度的副热带高压带有关的
senses.example: The subtropical high brings settled, dry weather in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 副热带高压在夏季带来稳定干燥的天气。
senses.why: Meteorology names the pressure belt by the latitude zone where it sits.
senses.whyCN: 气象学按气压带所在的纬度地带为其命名。

senses.title: A subtropical cyclone
senses.titleCN: 副热带气旋的：兼具热带与中纬度特征的气旋
senses.definition: describing a cyclone that shares features of tropical and mid-latitude systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述兼具热带与中纬度特征的气旋
senses.example: A subtropical cyclone can form over cooler water than a tropical one.
senses.exampleCN: 副热带气旋可在比热带气旋更冷的水面上形成。
senses.why: The storm mixes tropical and mid-latitude behaviour, so the prefix marks the in-between position.
senses.whyCN: 这种风暴混合了热带与中纬度行为，因此前缀标出居中的位置。

senses.title: Subtropical crops
senses.titleCN: 亚热带作物的：属于亚热带农业的
senses.definition: relating to crops grown in warm, frost-free belts outside the tropics
senses.definitionCN: 与热带外侧温暖无霜地带的作物有关的
senses.example: Subtropical crops include tea, citrus and olives.
senses.exampleCN: 亚热带作物包括茶、柑橘与油橄榄。
senses.why: Crops follow the climate, and the zone's frost-free warmth supports citrus and tea.
senses.whyCN: 作物随气候分布，这条带无霜的暖意支撑柑橘与茶。

senses.title: The subtropical jet
senses.titleCN: 副热带急流的：副热带高空强风带的
senses.definition: relating to the strong upper-air wind belt found near the edge of the tropics
senses.definitionCN: 与热带边缘附近的高空强风带有关的
senses.example: The subtropical jet steers winter storms across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 副热带急流引导冬季风暴穿过该地区。
senses.why: The jet runs along the edge of the tropical belt, so it takes the same marginal label.
senses.whyCN: 急流沿热带边缘运行，因此带着同样的「边缘」标签。

senses.title: The subtropics as a region
senses.titleCN: 亚热带地区：把该地带当作地区
senses.definition: the regions lying just outside the tropics, taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 热带外侧各地带的总称
senses.example: The subtropics are home to many of the world's largest coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 亚热带地区是世界许多最大沿海城市的所在地。
senses.why: Once a belt is named, its plural can stand for the places inside it.
senses.whyCN: 地带一旦有了名称，其复数形式就可以指带内的各个地方。

senses.title: Subtropical vegetation
senses.titleCN: 亚热带植被的：常绿阔叶与棕榈混生的
senses.definition: describing the mixed evergreen and palm vegetation of warm marginal belts
senses.definitionCN: 描述温暖边缘地带常绿阔叶与棕榈混生的植被
senses.example: Subtropical vegetation mixes palms with broadleaf trees.
senses.exampleCN: 亚热带植被把棕榈与阔叶树混在一起。
senses.why: Vegetation is the visible signature of the zone's warmth.
senses.whyCN: 植被是这条带暖意最可见的标志。

intro.en: Subtropical is Latin sub- 'under, near' joined to tropical. The term belongs to nineteenth-century geography and climatology, when the globe was divided into tropical, subtropical and temperate belts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subtropical 是拉丁 sub-「在下、靠近」加 tropical。这个词属于 19 世纪地理学与气候学，当时全球被划为热带、亚热带与温带。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below, close to'; in compounds it marks a position just short of the main thing.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于、靠近」；在复合词中表示略低于或紧邻主要事物。

items.en: The second element is the tropic adjective from Greek tropikos 'of a turn', the line where the sun reverses.
items.cn: 第二个成分是来自希腊 tropikos「转折的」的 tropic 形容词，指太阳折返的线。

items.en: Geographers divided the globe into tropical, subtropical, temperate and polar belts, and subtropical named the margin just outside the tropics.
items.cn: 地理学家把全球划为热带、亚热带、温带与极地，subtropical 指热带外侧的边缘。

items.en: Twentieth-century meteorology added the subtropical high, the subtropical jet and the subtropical cyclone.
items.cn: 20 世纪气象学增添了副热带高压、副热带急流与副热带气旋。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): no precise first English citation is recorded for the climate term, though its formation is transparent; the Latin and Greek roots are certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这一气候词在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录，但其构词透明；拉丁与希腊词根可靠。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like subtropical; group two holds neighbouring climate terms it is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 subtropical 的词；第二组是容易与之混淆的邻近气候词。

entries.definition: Belonging to the belt between the tropics; subtropical is the margin outside it.
entries.definitionCN: 属于两条回归线之间的地带；subtropical 是它外面的边缘。

entries.definition: A rare shortened adjective with the same meaning as subtropical.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的缩短形容词，意义与 subtropical 相同。

entries.definition: The regions just outside the tropics, taken as a place rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 热带外侧的地区，指地方而非性质。

entries.definition: Either of the two parallels where the sun turns; it is the boundary, not the belt beyond.
entries.definitionCN: 太阳折返的两条纬线之一；它是边界，不是外面的带。

entries.definition: Partly tropical in character, often used loosely for warm marginal zones.
entries.definitionCN: 性质上部分属热带，常用于宽泛地指温暖的边缘地带。

entries.definition: A temperate zone with mild winters, lying beyond the subtropics.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季温和的温带，位于亚热带之外。

entries.definition: Neither hot nor cold; it begins where the subtropical margin ends.
entries.definitionCN: 既不热也不冷；从亚热带边缘结束处开始。

entries.definition: The old name for the belt between the tropics, stressing heat rather than position.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时对回归线之间地带的称呼，强调炎热而非位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real sub- prefix, real climate belts and real meteorology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 sub- 前缀、真实的气候带与真实的气象学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Sub- 'near' + tropical: the belt that is nearly, but not quite, tropical.
normal.cn: sub-「靠近」+ tropical：几乎算热带、但还不算热带的带。

normal.en: Subtropical climate means hot summers and mild winters, good for citrus.
normal.cn: 亚热带气候意为夏热冬暖，适合柑橘。

normal.en: The subtropical high is a belt of dry descending air near thirty degrees latitude.
normal.cn: 副热带高压是约三十度纬度附近一条干爽的下沉气流带。

normal.en: The subtropics hold many coastal megacities.
normal.cn: 亚热带地区拥有许多沿海大城市。

normal.en: Subtropical vegetation mixes palms and broadleaf trees.
normal.cn: 亚热带植被把棕榈与阔叶树混生在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a warm room next to a hot room, sharing one wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一间温暖的房间紧挨着一间炎热的房间，共用一堵墙。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside where oranges grow but snow still visits once a year.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山坡，柑橘能长，但每年仍会下一次雪。

abstract.en: Picture a map with a soft border rather than a sharp line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，边界是柔和的过渡而不是硬线。

examples.en: The city has a subtropical climate with humid summers.
examples.cn: 这座城市属亚热带气候，夏季潮湿。

examples.en: Subtropical fruits such as lychee grow in the south.
examples.cn: 荔枝等亚热带水果在南方生长。

examples.en: The subtropical high dominated the weather for weeks.
examples.cn: 副热带高压连续数周主导天气。

dict_mnemonic.text: sub（在下、靠近）+ tropical（热带的）→ 靠近热带 → 亚热带的

root: 拉丁 sub-「在下、靠近」+ tropical；tropical 来自 tropic（希腊 tropikos「转折的」）+ -al，指热带外侧的温暖地带。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place one adjective just outside the tropics: the latitude belt, its mild climate, the high-pressure and jet systems, cyclones, crops, the region as a noun, and its mixed vegetation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把同一个形容词放在热带外侧：纬度带、温和气候、高压与急流系统、气旋、作物、作为名词的地区，以及混生植被。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm hillside just beyond the line where the sun turns, close to the tropics but not inside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：紧贴太阳折返线外侧的一片温暖山坡，靠近热带却不在其中。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the belt and the region it forms when taken as a whole.
branches.cn: 地方：这条带，以及把它整体看待时形成的地区。

branches.en: CLIMATE AND LIFE: mild warmth supports crops and a mixed evergreen vegetation.
branches.cn: 气候与生命：温和的暖意支撑作物与混生常绿植被。

branches.en: THE AIR: the subtropical high and subtropical jet are the belt's large-scale wind systems.
branches.cn: 空气：副热带高压与副热带急流是这条带的大尺度风系。

branches.en: STORMS: a subtropical cyclone mixes tropical and mid-latitude behaviour.
branches.cn: 风暴：副热带气旋混合了热带与中纬度的行为。

branches.en: AGRICULTURE: citrus, tea and olives mark the zone in farming.
branches.cn: 农业：柑橘、茶与油橄榄在农耕上标出这条带。

intro.en: Subtropical is a transparent compound of a Latin prefix and the adjective tropical; its family includes the noun subtropics and the rare short form subtropic.
intro.cn: subtropical 是拉丁前缀与形容词 tropical 构成的透明复合词；其词族包括名词 subtropics 与罕见短形式 subtropic。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub 'under, near' attaches to tropicus 'of the solstice'; English builds subtropical, subtropics and subtropically on that base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sub「在下、靠近」加在 tropicus「至点的」上；英语由此构成 subtropical、subtropics 与 subtropically。

items.example: The prefix marks a position just short of the tropics.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出略未达到热带的位置。

items.example: The second element is the tropic adjective.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分是 tropic 形容词。

items.example: Tropical air lies closer to the equator.
The short form appears in older botanical writing.
items.exampleCN: 这一短形式见于较早的植物学文字。

items.example: Subtropical rain fell for three days.
items.exampleCN: 亚热带降雨持续了三天。

items.example: The subtropics supply much of the world's tea.
items.exampleCN: 亚热带地区供应世界大部分茶叶。

items.example: The valley is subtropically warm in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷冬季暖如亚热带。
副极地低压驱动冬季风暴。

items.example: Subarctic forest gives way to tundra.
items.exampleCN: 亚北极森林过渡为苔原。

definition_en: an area outside a city where many people live
core_image: 城市边缘一圈低矮的房子和安静的街道
scene: 他们住在城市的郊区。They live in a suburb of the city.
sceneCN: 这里 suburb 是「郊区」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们住在城市的郊区。

senses.title: Edge of a city
senses.definition: a residential area outside the centre of a city
senses.definitionCN: 城市中心之外的住宅区
senses.example: They live in a suburb of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在城市的郊区。
senses.why: This is the basic geographic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的地理义项。

senses.title: Outlying districts
senses.definition: the outer districts of a city taken together
senses.definitionCN: 合起来指城市外围的区域
senses.example: Housing in the suburbs is cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 郊区的住房更便宜。
senses.why: The plural names the whole outer ring.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式指整个外围地带。

intro.en: Suburb joins Latin sub, under, with urbs, city.
intro.cn: suburb 由拉丁语 sub（在下）与 urbs（城市）组合而成。

items.en: Urbs meant a city.
items.cn: urbs 意为城市。

items.en: Suburbium meant the area below the city walls.
items.cn: suburbium 指城墙之外的区域。

items.en: Suburbe named the outer part of a town.
items.cn: suburbe 指城镇的外围。

items.en: Suburb named a residential area outside a city.
items.cn: suburb 指城市之外的住宅区。

items.en: The suburbs named the whole outer ring.
items.cn: the suburbs 指整个外围地带。

note.en: Suburb is compared with look-alike words and with words for city edges.
note.cn: 把 suburb 与形近词以及表示城市边缘的词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: suburb 就在城墙外不远处，近得可以通勤。

normal.cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。

normal.en: The train connects the suburb with the centre.
